_about: Rules for the Flow, cover and Cleanup audits, which run on backward chains (steam_layout/chains.py, covers.py, cleanups.py). The stacks are derived from the layout; this file only declares what bindings can't say: the starting contexts the chains may begin from (Base alone, and Base with the stateful Gyro layer on it), which layers are covers, and the exceptions register. Titles use default-layout names; 'variants' maps them for the alternative layout. Until 2026-10-01 this file also declared a 'families' section for the family walk (deprecated); that version is kept as archived/depth-search-and-family-walk/tests/data/flow_families_90.9.json.

covers._about: Cover-type layers (Layer Definition of Done section 5). They inherit their owner, so differing lower bindings are expected; the cover check (covers.py) judges them instead.

exceptions_about: The exceptions register (steam_layout/exceptions.py): every place where the layout breaks a rule and that is accepted (status allow) or is a known gap a to-do will close (status todo). Each entry names its rule (resources/Layer Definition of Done.md), what it covers, why, who decided it and when, and the to-do that ends it. Until 2026-10-02 these lived in four shapes: 'decisions', 'covers.allow' and 'cleanups.keep' here, and per-target decisions in traced_stacks.json. An entry that matches nothing is reported as stale by the audit that reads it.

exceptions.why: 90.43: the author chose to protect the first movement after centered Steering entry, including while either thumb rests or lifts. Entry Guard therefore carries only each stick's ordinary helper Release cleanup, with no automatic guard removal. A direction/normal outer-edge Release, driver acquisition or fresh menu Start Press consumes it. Pad-helper and ramp entries are blocked while it is present. The exact Entry Guard title, presence of Stateful Fn and absence of Fallback Hold exclude the frozen pre-90.33 Entry Guard implementations (plans/2026-10-09-steering-entry-guard.md).
exceptions.decided: Author approved implementation, 2026-10-09

exceptions.why: 90.43: Entry Guard deliberately protects the first movement. Its normal left-stick outer-edge Release disarms it; unconditional active-edge cleanup would end protection on the first push. Since 90.44 its inverted left-edge chord additionally removes only the guard while either driver is held, under the exact R111 exception; centered entry without a driver remains protected. Its right-stick edge is blocked so camera movement cannot remove protection or add a ramp over the left-stick Releases. Direction Releases and explicit driver/menu handoffs remain exits. This exact guard scope requires Stateful Fn and excludes Fallback Hold, so historical Entry Guards keep their original edge rule (plans/2026-10-10-entry-guard-edge-and-quiet-drivers.md).
exceptions.decided: Author approved implementation, 2026-10-09; driver-conditioned inward exit, 2026-10-10

exceptions.why: These removes are needed, and the audit's chains cannot see it. A stick's Tap Cover and Temporary Gyro come on by a delayed add, which the chains do not follow, so the Cleanup audit calls them never there with a Stateful Entry Point. On the simulator they were on the stack when the Entry Point's stick click Release fired (findings/2026-10-12-remove-list-audit: 48,000 random walks a layout). Since 90.58 the fourteen clears name only what can be on the stack (R163), the check applies to them, and the cleanup_lists fix would take these sixteen removes out. The entry goes stale when the chains follow a delayed add; on a layout up to 90.57 it is unused.

scope.note: Menu Keys has no Entry Points. It blocks Start and Select, and a chord on each stick click, on Start or Select being held, runs the Entry Points' clear list and adds the clear transition, as in Gamepad. It fires at the click's press, not its Release.

exceptions.why: An Entry Point's tap opens a Double Tap window. A window that can land on Menu Keys would have to clear the face buttons and the D-pad on every stack, Base included, because Menu Keys has a layer command on them: its stick-plus-button exit (R140). Without Entry Points no window lands there. The plan had the shared Stateful Entry Points; the author asked for the exit, a menu button plus a stick click, not for how it is built. If the menu button is let go before the stick click, Base is live under a held click and may type one Q or E (A11).

The left stick being out is what keeps these two layers on, so nothing can guard a cleanup function on its edge. The Entry Guard's exits are the edge Release and, since 90.31, each direction's Release; the Fallback Hold's are the up and down Releases since 90.30. Their cleanup function goes on the right-stick edge, guarded by the left stick being out. Both layers are gone in 90.33 (the Entry Guard became the fallback guard, which binds no edge), so this holds only on a layout that still has the Fallback Hold: it stays for the frozen 90.24 to 90.32 builds, which read the register as they build.

Since 90.24 the cover has a right-stick group in mouse mode, for its stick-touch cleanup (R169). Over a layer whose right stick is in D-pad mode nothing on that stick is inherited (A2), so the cover hides this exit. The cover is only on while the right thumb rests on the right pad, and the hidden inputs need that thumb on the right stick. A stale cover removes itself on the right-stick touch. Called out by the author: while the thumb is on the pad, a menu button plus the right-stick click does not start a transition, in the Entry Points and in the Fn layers that inherit that click.

The chorded window sits on the Fn layer, which inherits both stick clicks from the Entry Point: the transition gestures. A window must not let a layer change through (R140), so it clears them for its 150 ms. The Entry Point's keeper is its menu button, and the window carries that button's Release: it removes the window first, then the Entry Point and the Fn layer. Nothing is left on.

The player sees the same thing in every stack: with the menu button held the input does what it did, and with it not held the stale menu layers are removed.

The second-press layer of a chorded chain sits on the Fn layer while the first menu button is held, and on Base once that button is let go: its Release takes the Fn layer's family and the held second button keeps this layer (the owner leaves, a held button falls through). exceptions.why: 90.38 additive fallback return: Steering normally inherits Base's empty WASD slot. When the requested fallback edge adds Steering without removing fallback, it inherits that same silent driver-conditioned repeat adding already-active Steering. A3 makes the re-add idempotent; the inverted edge does not run at the rim. No output is displaced except Base's empty placeholder. Preserve this intentional inheritance and review the additive stack in the release scenarios. This decision applies only to layouts containing Fallback Guard; 90.43 reuses that slot as Entry Guard and removes the additive return.
exceptions.decided: Codex review of author-requested additive fallback edge, 2026-10-08

exceptions.why: 90.52: a Steering stick modifier's sequence runs on its own direction, as the bumper modifier's runs on its bumper, and that input carries no cleanup function (R130's left-out clause, as R171 leaves out a layer's own button). Up in the up modifier holds the 200 ms hold marker, its reset and the Release that opens the window; up in the scroll layer holds the scroll, the cover's 150 ms add, its reset and the Release back to the window. A driver release missed with the stick held in that direction is cleared by the next other input.

90.52: a Steering stick modifier's sequence runs on its own direction, as the bumper modifier's runs on its bumper, and that input carries no cleanup function (R130's left-out clause, as R171 leaves out a layer's own button). Down in the down modifier and in its scroll layer, as up in theirs. A driver release missed with the stick held in that direction is cleared by the next other input.

90.52: a Steering stick modifier's sequence runs on its own direction, as the bumper modifier's runs on its bumper, and that input carries no cleanup function (R130's left-out clause, as R171 leaves out a layer's own button). The hold marker and the cover serve both modifiers, so up and down are both their own direction: each has the Release that ends the hold, and the cover the repeating scroll. A driver release missed with the stick held in that direction is cleared by the next other input.

90.72: the right-pad click layers bind only the right pad and the sticks' touches and edges, and pass every other input through. Since 90.72 the Steering stick layers and their covers add the Click Entry Point on the right-pad click (the stand-ins for their left-edge timers), so the chains put these layers over the Steering stacks, where the face buttons, D-pad, Start, Select, stick clicks and left-stick directions come from whichever Steering layer is under them. 90.71 already put them there through Base's click; the chains did not see it. Inheriting is the intent (author, 2026-10-14: plans/2026-10-14-pad-stick-edge-cleanups.md).

These removes are needed, and the audit's chains cannot see it. Since 90.72 the Stateful Entry Points block both pad clicks and bind the right pad's touch, so no pad layer can land on top of them, and the cleanup_lists fix reads that as these layers never being there. They are, underneath: a click or Circular Scroll that is on before Start or Select stays under the Entry Point that lands on top. On the simulator they were on the stack when the Entry Point's stick click Release fired (tests/test_scenarios_90_58.py, Clears: 240 random walks a layout; Circular Scroll by a direct sequence: scroll, hold Start, click a stick).
exceptions.decided: Claude, 2026-10-14, on the 90.58 clear check against 90.72 (plans/2026-10-14-pad-stick-edge-cleanups.md); follows the author's rule that a clear names every layer that can be on the stack (R163)

exceptions.why: 90.72: every layer that blocks the right pad's click binds the pad's touch to a Release that removes the right pad's touch layers (author, 2026-10-14). The two menu stick guards bind no pad and inherit that Release from the menu Entry Point under them. Its list depends on which Entry Point: the plain ones name RTP: Entry Point, RTP: Tap Cover and RTP: Circular Scroll, the Stateful ones only RTP: Entry Point, as the cleanup rules find what can be under each. Either way a lift clears the right pad's touch layers that are there.
exceptions.decided: Claude, 2026-10-14, reading the Flow audit for 90.72 under the author's rule above (plans/2026-10-14-pad-stick-edge-cleanups.md); not yet confirmed by the author

exceptions.why: Ibex 1.1: the stick clicks' Releases, the transitions, moved from the Stateful Entry Points to their Fn layers, command for command, because each Fn adder now removes its Entry Point (plans/2026-10-16-fn-right-stick-owner.md, part 3). The two entries above keep these ten removes in the Entry Points' Releases, and their reasons hold here: a stick's Tap Cover and Temporary Gyro come on by a delayed add, which the chains do not follow, and a pad click layer or Circular Scroll that is on before Start or Select stays underneath, where nothing in the chains shows it. Fn lands on what was under its Entry Point, so the same layers are under it. Without this the cleanup_lists fix takes all ten out of both Releases of both layers. On a layout before Ibex 1.1 the Stateful Fn layers have no click Release and the entry is unused.
exceptions.decided: Claude, 2026-10-16, building the author's design (plans/2026-10-16-fn-right-stick-owner.md); follows the two entries for the Stateful Entry Points
